claims.text: The precursor targets an equiatomic Hf-Nb-Ta-Ti-Zr alloy.
The green compact has an initial oxygen content below 0.5 wt%.
TaH0.5, NbH, HfH2, TiH2, and ZrH2 undergo sequential thermal decomposition during heating.
A dispersed Zr metal getter under ultra-high vacuum scavenges oxygen released during hydride decomposition.
The Zr getter reacts preferentially with oxygen to form stable ZrO2 precipitates.
Hydride decomposition releases hydrogen and increases local oxygen activity.
Lowering oxygen partial pressure with the getter suppresses nucleation of alpha-HCP phases.
Oxygen dissolved in the BCC lattice would stabilize an alpha-HCP phase.
Rapid cooling suppresses diffusion-controlled decomposition of the beta-BCC phase by bypassing a eutectoid transformation window.
Rapid quenching from approximately 1300-1400 °C will retain a metastable single-phase beta-BCC structure.
The quenched microstructure will have less than 1% porosity.
The quenched microstructure will have a grain size of 2-10 µm.
The final oxygen content will be below 0.2 wt%.
The final alloy will have hardness above 400 HV.
The quenched material will have greater ductility than slow-cooled counterparts.
No detectable alpha-HCP or Ti-rich alpha phase will remain after quenching.
Sintering without a getter or with slower cooling produces an HCP-containing or otherwise multiphase microstructure.
The HCP phase formed in the baseline is Zr/Hf-rich.
The critical hydride decomposition window is approximately 600-900 °C.
An increase in the BCC lattice parameter indicates oxygen occupying interstitial sites.

contradictions.description: The getter is said to generate ZrO2 precipitates, yet the outcome is called a single-phase beta-BCC solid solution; the falsification rule further permits ZrO2 as a secondary phase.

Adding dispersed Zr powder to an already equiatomic Hf-Nb-Ta-Ti-Zr blend changes the alloy composition unless the getter is external or its amount is included in the equiatomic balance, neither of which is specified.
The main hypothesis specifically requires ultra-high vacuum below 10^-6 Pa, whereas the conditions also permit high-purity argon with a Zr getter.
